status_summary: The modernization strand is underway through appropriations rather than the structural changes the Mandate lists. Congress provided $12.5 billion in Public Law 119-21, signed 2025-07-04 (Sec. 40003; DOT calls it the Working Families Tax Cut Act), for a new air traffic control system that DOT announced on 2025-05-08 and says will be deployed by the end of 2028. On 2026-09-28 Senator Eric Schmitt introduced the Modern Skies Act, a $30 billion second phase that DOT and the FAA Administrator endorsed; DOT's FY2027 budget request (released 2026-04-03) asks $4.0 billion for FAA Facilities and Equipment, flat with FY2026. None of the DOT materials, the Modern Skies Act draft text or news coverage reviewed mentions separating the ATO from the FAA, replacing taxes with fees for air traffic services, or revenue bonds.

timeline.event: DOT announces a plan to build a new air traffic control system covering communications, surveillance, automation and facilities (telecommunications upgrades at over 4,600 sites, replacement of 618 radars, six new air traffic control centers and replacement of towers and approach control facilities). The release does not mention separating the Air Traffic Organization, user fees or governance changes.

Public Law 119-21 (H.R. 1) is enacted; its table of contents lists Sec. 40003, 'Air traffic control improvements,' and a White House fact sheet says the law provides $12.5 billion to modernize air traffic control systems, retire aging equipment, hire and train controllers and consolidate outdated facilities, without mentioning separation of the Air Traffic Organization or user fees. DOT calls the law the Working Families Tax Cut Act and, in a 2025-06-26 op-ed, called the $12.5 billion a down payment and said more money would be needed.

DOT releases its FY2027 budget request. The Budget Highlights request $4.0 billion for FAA Facilities and Equipment, flat with FY2026 (about $1.5 billion of it for the new air traffic control system), describe it as complementing the $12.5 billion provided in FY2025, and propose no reorganization of the air traffic organization and no new air traffic user fees (release date from DOT's budget page; the Highlights page was last updated 2026-05-05).

Senator Eric Schmitt introduces the Modern Skies Act (DOT's release says it was introduced that day); the Senate-hosted draft text, which shows a blank bill number, appropriates about $30 billion for FY2027 in three parts: $10 billion for a pilot to modernize or rebuild terminals at up to three transitional hub airports, $10.1 billion to the FAA (including $7.2 billion for a common automation platform and controller workstation, $2 billion for cloud computing infrastructure, $600 million for traffic flow management technology and $300 million to consolidate terminal air traffic control facilities), and $10 billion for terminal air traffic control facilities (including digital tower technology) and airport grants. It would also let the FAA Administrator transfer funds among the paragraphs of section 40003(a) of Public Law 119-21. The draft does not mention an Air Traffic Organization separation, user fees, bonds or changes to FAA governance. DOT and the FAA Administrator endorse it; DOT says first-phase deployment should finish by the end of 2028. No committee action was found.
DOT fact sheet on the Modern Skies Act breaks down the $30 billion and does not mention an Air Traffic Organization, user fees, bonds or governance changes.

The absence of any structural reform (ATO separation, user fees, revenue bonds) rests on DOT materials, Nextgov, FedScoop and AOPA coverage plus two web searches (one returned only 2017 first-term material); congressional bills outside those sources were not enumerated. The FY2027 $4.0 billion Facilities and Equipment figure is from DOT's Budget Highlights (pp. 15-16 as read), which FedScoop also cites; the statement that the Highlights propose no reorganization of the air traffic organization and no new user fee comes from a tool summary of the document, not a line-by-line read.
